As soldiers in Hashem’s Army, we know that every Yid has a precious and loveable neshama inside. But the Yetzer Hara tries to trick us by saying that “what we see is what we get”: the way someone looks and acts is exactly who they are. The sneaky enemy tells us that if a Yid doesn’t do good things, then he’s not good (or at least, he’s not as good as us). The Yetzer Hara wants us to focus on the “חיצוניות — outer layer” and be judgmental (which means “judging negatively”), instead of looking for the Yid’s “פנימיות — inner layer”, their neshama, and judging positively.

Recon Mission

Getting to know the enemy’s weapons and tactics before planning

In a war, the first step toward victory is to expose the enemy’s strategy. This way, we avoid falling into his trap. In Tzivos Hashem we face the trickiest enemy: the Yetzer Hara.

Here’s his strategy: First, the Yetzer Hara plants negative thoughts in our heads. Then, those thoughts grow into worse feelings that can lead to even more dangerous actions.

Look at the following scene and identify where the Yetzer Hara could convince you to be judgmental and trigger your thoughts, speech, and actions.

We have just uncovered another one of the Yetzer Hara’s tricks! He tries convincing us that who someone is on the outside is their true self, and we should judge them in that way.

Discuss a time when each squad member fell into the enemy’s trap of judgmental behavior because they felt dismissive, critical, or superior. Identify the thoughts that caused those feelings.

Don't forget to include Torah, tefillah, tzedakah, and Moshiach in your meeting!

See you next week to learn this battle’s strategy from Rivka Imeinu.
